evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useApi.ts:83-92 — the central online client `apiRequest()` throws a bare `new Error(\`HTTP ${response.status}\`)` on any non-ok response and has NO 401 -> refresh -> retry interception. `useApiQuery` (107-117) and `useApiMutation` (142-155) both flow through it, so when the access token expires while the app is foregrounded, every query/mutation fails with `HTTP 401` even though a valid refresh_token sits in SecureStore unused.

There is no global recovery either: frontend/apps/mobile/src/App.tsx:47-55 configures the QueryClient with only `staleTime`/`gcTime`/`retry: 3` and no `QueryCache`/`MutationCache` `onError`, and grep for `refreshToken()` / `refreshAccessToken` inside hooks/useApi.ts returns nothing. `retry: 3` actually makes it worse — a 401 is re-sent 3 times with the same expired bearer before surfacing.

The app already knows how to do this on the OTHER path: frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:34 lists 401 in `RETRYABLE_HTTP_STATUSES` and comments (lines 20, 281-285) that a 401 replay 'replays with a refreshed token'. AuthContext.refreshToken() (contexts/AuthContext.tsx:174-211) exists but is only invoked at session restore (jwt staleness) and after biometric re-auth (275, 326) — never reactively from the online request path and with no AppState/interval proactive timer. Effect: a session left open past the (short, per docs/api) access-token TTL degrades into wall-to-wall error banners until the user backgrounds/relaunches or re-logs-in. Fix: wrap apiRequest so a 401 triggers a single-flight refresh + one retry (and exclude non-retryable 4xx from `retry: 3`).

frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/ — the NFC access-credential subsystem has ZERO test coverage: `find frontend/apps/mobile -name '*.test.*' | grep -i nfc` returns nothing, while ~48 other feature/screen modules ship co-located tests (AnnouncementsScreen, VotingScreen, useOfflineSupport, jwt, deepLinkRouting, etc.).

The untested code is security-sensitive and does non-trivial persistence/branching: NFCCredentialManager.ts handles physical building-access credentials — loadStoredCredentials() (262-290) parses SecureStore JSON, discards-on-corruption, and runs a one-time AsyncStorage->SecureStore legacy migration (278-289); storeCredentials() (292-294) serializes the whole credential list into a single SecureStore value; usageCount is bumped + persisted (255-256); apiRequest() (296-320) fetches credentials from the backend. NFCAccessController.ts adds wallet/encrypted-data handling (see the `credential has no encrypted data` guard at NFCAccessController.ts:376).

These are exactly the corruption-recovery, migration, and credential-fetch paths whose regressions are silent (a bad migration or a discarded blob just means 'no access credentials') and security-relevant. Fix: add unit tests for loadStoredCredentials corruption + legacy-migration branches and for the encrypted-data guard, mocking expo-secure-store / AsyncStorage.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:97-107 (login) and :194-200 (refreshToken) read `data.access_token` / `data.refresh_token` straight off `await response.json()` after only an `!response.ok` check, then immediately `SecureStore.setItemAsync(ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY, accessToken)` with no assertion that the fields are present strings. A 200 response with a malformed/partial body (upstream proxy, shape drift) writes `undefined` into SecureStore.

Downstream that poisons every request: hooks/useApi.ts:67 builds `Authorization: \`Bearer ${accessToken}\`` from the stored token, so a stored `undefined`/`'undefined'` yields `Bearer undefined` on all calls and a confusing auth-failure loop rather than a clean login error. On some platforms `SecureStore.setItemAsync(key, undefined)` also throws, turning a bad-body login into an unhandled rejection inside the try (login's catch at 92-95 only covers `!response.ok`).

This is the same 'a 200 does not guarantee a well-formed body' hardening the reality-web listings path already applies (page.tsx routes bodies through parseListingDetail before use). Fix: after parsing, assert `typeof access_token === 'string' && typeof refresh_token === 'string'` (and for login, `user`) before persisting; throw a normal login/refresh error otherwise so the existing catch + logout path handles it.
